# `⍪` — Table / Catenate first

Function. Keys: `Alt-Minus ,`. Hanzi: `接/矩`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `∞ ∞` dyadic

`⍪Y` makes a matrix: first axis becomes rows, remaining axes become columns.

```bpl
⍪1 2 3             ⍝ 3 1ρ1 2 3
ρ⍪2 3 4ρ0          ⍝ [2 12]ₓ
```

`X⍪Y` joins on the first axis. `⍪⍠K` follows [catenate](comma.qmd).

```bpl
1 2⍪3 4            ⍝ 1 2 3 4
```

## Inverse

`⍪⁻Y` gives the vector that a one-column matrix holds, and gives back any other matrix. `X⍪⁻Y` removes the fixed major cells `X` from the front of `Y`. With the right argument fixed, `(⍪↢X)⁻Y` removes them from the end.

```bpl
⍪⁻⍪1 2 3             ⍝ 1 2 3
[1 2]⍪⁻[1 2◇3 4]   ⍝ [3 4◇]
```
